title: Build a statistical sign and offset detector for every dataset
status_note: GT24 pilot done (detector efd74e73, rule B): 0 wrong signs; README ankle sign never applied (conflict in all 40 legs); data only, ankle moment applied +1 in 40/40. UM21 and GT23 pilots done earlier. GT21 pilot remains.
summary: Dataset-agnostic detector for sagittal channels under rule B (D-UM21-C03-1 = B: segments counterclockwise; joint angles and internal moments positive in their named direction). Tests: reference angle from markers or independent segments (strong); quasi-static GRF lever arm (ankle strong, knee moderate, hip weak); late-stance plantarflexor moment (moderate, forward tasks); knee hinge asymmetry (moderate, walking only); segment chain and power identity (strong relations, one-hop propagation); cited template (weak, never applies); documentation (blocks on disagreement, never applies); 180-degree branch screen (masks frames from fits, never edits). Verdicts are apply/suggest/conflict/abstain from fixed scores; only apply signs are applied. Offsets are estimated (median of sign*source - reference, bootstrap 95% CI, seed 20261030) and flagged, never applied.

required_fixes.fix: New plate_frame_check: CoP progression heel->toe relative to the ankle, and braking then propulsion of the anterior GRF. If CoP progression fails, the lever arm abstains. If it is unknown (no ankle positions), the ankle lever arm is downgraded to moderate and cannot apply alone. If braking/propulsion fails, the anterior GRF is dropped. Results are in report.plate_frame_check and the lever_arm stats. The design-note claim that marker angles catch a reversed plate frame was removed.

_propagate now resolves contradictions first, then derives one hop from a snapshot of the channels still applied. Conflicted channels are neither anchors nor targets, so the result is order-independent.

vertical_order_fraction plus marker_reference_angles raise ValueError when hip above knee above ankle holds in fewer than 90% of frames. detect_leg(marker_points=...) records marker_checks and uses no marker reference on failure. The design note now limits the invariance claim to a correct up vector.

Offset differences are wrapped to (-pi, pi] per sample and per unit. Also, 360-degree wraps are re-expressed within +-180 deg of the channel median in the fitting copy instead of being masked (same angle; source unchanged).

recommendations_done: An angle channel with |value| > 2*pi is refused (units_check), not fitted: test_degree_input_is_refused_not_fitted.

The branch screen masks only runs bounded by a one-sample jump above 90 deg, or runs filling a whole unit. Continuous excursions are reported as far_from_median_frames and not masked: test_deep_flexion_is_not_a_branch.
stance_from_grf has an absolute floor of 0.5 N/kg: test_stance_floor_rejects_contact_free_unit.
The design note requires the forward axis per straight pass (or per unit) for out-and-back or turning trials.

verification_round_2.structural_change: No sign is applied from a single test. combine() needs agreeing moderate/strong tests from at least min_families=2 evidence families (score >= 2). A single test, or several tests from one family, gives at most 'suggest'. Families come from FAMILY_GROUPINGS: 'coarse' (default, the coordinator's rule) = kinematic {reference angle, knee hinge, segment chain} / force_plate {lever arm, late stance} / power_identity. 'fine' (offered for review only) = marker_geometry / joint_anatomy / plate_geometry / plate_timing / power_identity. Template, documentation and unclassified tests have no family.

what_still_reaches_apply.fine (default): Synthetic clinical fixture: knee angle -1 (marker geometry + joint anatomy) and ankle moment +1 (plate geometry + plate timing) are applied. Pelvis -1, hip +1, ankle +1 angles and knee moment -1 are 'suggest' with the correct sign. Hip moment and all powers abstain.
what_still_reaches_apply.coarse (option): Nothing can reach apply with the current tests (angles have only kinematic tests, moments only force-plate tests, power derives only from applied channels).

required_fixes.fix: plate_frame_check runs both checks only for COP_PROGRESSION_TASKS (level/incline/decline walking). For any other task, including None, backward walking, running and stair descent, they are 'unknown', so the ankle lever arm stays moderate. The design-note sentence about forefoot strikers and toe walkers is corrected.

required_fixes.fix: _propagate step 1 judges every relation against one snapshot taken before any change, and marks every member of every contradicting relation. Contradictions now also cover 'suggest' signs, not only 'apply'.
required_fixes.evidence: verify::test_every_contradicting_relation_is_honoured passes. Under min_families=1, all three channels are 'conflict'. The worker propagation test covers both relation orders.

required_fixes.fix: vertical_order_fraction now checks that pelvis markers, hip and knee are above the foot point (ankle, else heel, else toe); this also covers recommendation 1. required_fixes.fix: Source and reference are each re-expressed within +-pi of their own robust circular centre (median after re-expressing around the circular mean). Own centres are used rather than a common one, because a sign-flipped source has the opposite centre. An offset above pi/2 in magnitude gives a 'conflict' verdict with the reason 'half-turn offset: branch or zero-definition mismatch'.
required_fixes.evidence: verify near-pi and half-turn tests pass. Under min_families=1, the near-pi case applies +1 with offset 0.0, and the branch-majority case is 'conflict' (half-turn, -3.14 rad).

recommendations_done: Vertical order uses 'above the foot' rather than hip above knee, as described in fix 3.

The stance floor is unit-aware: stance_from_grf(grf, unit) uses floors of 0.5 N/kg, 0.05 BW or 20 N, with no mass needed, and refuses an undeclared unit. detect_leg(grf_unit=...) is required to derive stance; otherwise the force-plate tests abstain with the reason 'not declared'.
The reference-angle test abstains when the median |slope| is outside [0.1, 10] or any |value| exceeds 2*pi (units).

proposed_decision.question: May the sign detector change a channel's sign automatically when two tests with different failure modes agree (for example, markers plus knee range of motion, or lever arm plus late-stance timing)?
proposed_decision.why: In 20 UMich legs (10 recordings), the two family pairs never disagreed with each other or with the known signs: knee angle applied in 16 legs and ankle moment in 20, all right. In the verifier's independent run (AB04/d10, CoP registered at the heel marker at contact, about 11 cm behind the midpoint rule), the ankle lever arm voted the wrong sign in both legs. The CoP-within-foot check did not stop it: it returned 'unknown', because only 73% and 82% of strides fell inside the +-3 cm band, short of the 90% needed to decide. The pair returned a conflict only because the late-stance test disagreed. The check therefore catches CoP registration errors only above about 11 cm; smaller registration errors rely on the second family. Only one dataset (Vicon treadmill) has been tested; GT21, GT23 and GT24 should confirm before any release use.

marker_reference_angles returns MarkerAngle ndarray values that carry vertical_order. detect_leg drops every MarkerAngle reference whose check is not 'pass', and records this in marker_checks.dropped. dict(), key selection and slicing keep the guard; only an explicit np.asarray removes it (documented).

grf_unit_check: the median per-unit peak vertical GRF must lie within 0.4-4 BW in the declared unit (N_per_kg x9.81; BW; N x9.81 x declared mass, or a 30-200 kg band if no mass is declared). On failure, the GRF, CoP and stance inputs are discarded, so every force-plate test abstains with the reason 'implausible'. The result is in report.grf_unit_check. The new detect_leg argument is body_mass_kg (optional).

rule_b_retarget.detector: TARGET_CONVENTION is rule B (rule_id "B"). New JOINT_CCW = {hip: +1, knee: -1, ankle: +1}: joint angle = JOINT_CCW x (distal - proximal segment); internal moment = JOINT_CCW x the counterclockwise moment on the distal segment. Marker knee angle = thigh - shank; segment chain shank = thigh - knee (the fitted joint coefficient is multiplied by JOINT_CCW before it becomes a relation); knee lever arm x -1 (knee flexor positive); the knee hinge now expects the large excursion on the positive side. phase3_verifier_fix.problem: A hip-angle column from the other leg (half-cycle shift) looked negated to both the marker test and hip stance extension, so marker geometry + plate timing applied a wrong sign; the knee-based leg gate did not see it.
phase3_verifier_fix.choice_logged: Combined the lag check with a family rule (options 2 + family collapse). Every reference-waveform test (marker reference angle, lever arm, ID-light) also fits the channel shifted by half a unit and compares the median |r| with lag 0 (margin 0.05, fixed in advance). Half-cycle lag better => the test abstains ('column from the other leg?'). Within the margin => the evidence is flagged half_cycle_ambiguous, and combine() counts it and all plate-timed tests as one family ('fixed_timing_shape'). Option 1 (the other leg's markers) and a per-channel shape gate were not used: for a pure sinusoid they cannot tell the other leg from negation either, while the family rule blocks it by construction.
phase3_verifier_fix.other_pairs_checked: Swept a half-cycle column shift over every channel that can apply (hip, knee and ankle angles; hip and ankle moments; ankle and hip power) with a pure-cosine and an asymmetric hip: no wrong apply. The knee is safe because the knee-range test reads the value distribution (shift-invariant). The ankle angle, ankle moment and hip moment are not antisymmetric, so their reference tests abstain on the shifted column. Powers need applied anchors.
phase3_verifier_fix.consequence: The pure-cosine fixture hip is now suggest only (previously apply); hip power then abstains. A hip with a 0.12 rad 2nd harmonic still applies. On real data, near-sinusoidal hips will mostly stay suggest; the pilot re-run will show how often.
